name: Evidence for neutrino emission from NGC 1068

significance.quote: We found an excess of $79_{-20}^{+22}$ neutrinos associated with the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068 at a significance of 4.2$\,\sigma$.

summary.plain: IceCube saw about 79 extra neutrinos coming from a nearby galaxy with a hidden, dust-shrouded black hole at its centre — far more neutrinos than the gamma rays from the same galaxy would suggest.
summary.technical: Point-source search over 2011–2020 data with improved reconstruction and calibration; 110 a priori gamma-ray sources analysed. An excess of 79(+22/-20) neutrinos at NGC 1068 with 4.2σ significance; the inferred TeV neutrino flux exceeds the TeV gamma-ray flux by at least an order of magnitude.

title: Evidence for neutrino emission from the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068
why_it_matters: First steady neutrino source candidate and evidence that neutrinos escape from environments opaque to gamma rays, probing the obscured core of an active galaxy.
